subject: general
question: Demetrius, a Bactrian-Greek ruler, came into conflict with ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pushyamitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pushyamitra** was the founder of the **Shunga Dynasty** in ancient India.
 
• He is historically known for overthrowing the **Mauryan dynasty** and establishing his rule around **185 BCE**.
 
• Pushyamitra Shunga was a **Brahmin general** in the Mauryan Empire before he ascended to power.
 
• He is believed to have engaged in conflicts with the **Bactrian-Greek ruler Demetrius I**, who invaded parts of northern India during his reign.
 
• Demetrius I's campaigns were aimed at expanding the Indo-Greek territories, leading to confrontations with local rulers, including Pushyamitra.
 
• The historical records, including texts like the **Milindapanha** and works by **classical historians**, suggest that these invasions were a significant challenge for the Shunga rulers.
 
• Pushyamitra's reign marked the decline of the **Buddhist influence** propagated by the Mauryan rulers and a resurgence of **Brahmanical practices**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harsha**__

 __
 
• **Harsha** was an emperor who ruled northern India during the **7th century CE**.
 
• He is known for his reign of peace, prosperity, and revival of **Hinduism and Buddhism**.
 
• Harsha was not contemporary to Demetrius or Pushyamitra, as his rule occurred much later.
 
 
 
• **Nahapana**__
 __
 
• **Nahapana** was a ruler of the **Western Kshatrapas**, a dynasty of Indo-Scythian origin.
 
• He ruled during the early centuries of the **Common Era**, much after the time of Demetrius and Pushyamitra.
 
• Hence, there was no direct conflict between Nahapana and Demetrius.
 
 
 
• **Simuka**__
 
 
• **Simuka** was the founder of the **Satavahana Dynasty**, ruling parts of South India.
 
• His reign was not contemporaneous with Demetrius, and his kingdom was geographically distant from the Indo-Greek territories.
